entries.report: More than approximately 64 distinct inventory records can cause silent item loss.
entries.note: 63/64/65 records across loot, transfer, purchase, save, and reload. Distinguish failure to insert from later serialization loss.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: A pack holds 64 stacks; adding a 65th stack that joins no existing stack is silently refused (R031+0x4A04). Buying (R032+0x0F60) charges the price before the add and taking an item from an inn store (R035+0x0A46) removes it from the store before the add, and neither screen tests for a full pack, so the item is lost. Loot moved into a full pack is already listed in the OriginalBehaviour remarks; transfers between members test for room first, and a save keeps all 64 entries, so the loss is at insertion, not in serialization.

entries.report: A stack quantity is structurally bounded by one byte; behavior of an attempted quantity 256 remains unknown.
entries.note: Test quantities 254/255 plus insertion, merge, split, transfer, consumption, and save/load. Do not state wrap, loss, or corruption without reproduction.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: A pack stack cannot pass 255: a join is made only when the total stays within 255, otherwise a new stack is started (R031+0x4A04). Two other counts are single bytes without that test: an inn store entry (already listed in the OriginalBehaviour remarks, see RPT-INN-0001) and the battle loot list, where a combatant who dies next to an existing pile has equal items added to the pile's entry in a byte (R014+0xE930), so a merged total above 255 wraps and the excess is lost.

entries.report: Aggregate inventory above 255 was proposed as a palette-corruption trigger.
entries.note: A character has only 64 record slots; the claim may conflate stack quantity, aggregate objects, inn indexing, or an unrelated palette copy defect. It is not an established trigger for `RPT-PALETTE-0001`.

check.label: Still open
check.note: No byte-sized aggregate of a character's or the party's items was found: the item counting routines sum into integers (R029+0x0C76) and a pack is at most 64 stacks of 255. The one overflow of an inventory-like table found in this check is the inn store's working table: a store with more than 100 different entries runs past it, and past 196 entries over memory that was not traced (D-674296). Whether that or anything else reaches the palette needs a runtime test in the original with stores of 100, 197 and 256 entries and the palette compared before and after.

entries.report: More than 255 items stored at an inn may be lost on retrieval.
entries.note: Inn-storage quantity/record layouts at 254/255/256 and retrieval compaction.

check.label: Reproduced, noted in the code
check.note: Reproduced: an inn store entry's count is a byte, so the 256th item of one kind and quality turns it to 0 and the 257th to 1 (R035+0x10D2). Taking from an entry at 0 hands out an item and leaves 255 (R035+0x114A), so exactly 256 items can all be taken back, but from 257 on the multiples of 256 are lost. Documented in the OriginalBehaviour remarks, no register id.

entries.report: Inn storage and enemy cloth drops stopped working in one long-running world; moving the party to a fresh world restored storage.
entries.note: Investigate world/event-table corruption or exhaustion separately from party records. Copying the old four-byte world RNG seed happened after storage was repaired and is not evidence that the seed caused or fixed the defect. “Storing cloth causes it” remains unsupported.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: The code has a mechanism by which inn storage in one long-running world breaks while a fresh world works: the store file only grows (a store emptied and given up stays in it); the append has no limit, so the 99th store's offset lands on the first store's bytes; and the rewrite of a known store finds the first store from the signed low byte of its offset and lays the file out with a 101-byte header over a 198-byte one, so the other stores are copied from the wrong place. The restoration reproduces all of this exactly in its faithful mode (registered as original bugs B-85e0e4, B-3de49c, B-cf6bdb; the whole-game session cache-revisit agrees with the original). In the player's game two switchable data-safety fixes are on by default (D-856386, D-2a45ce): the file is laid out compactly, as the original's own code reads and rewrites it without loss (up to 62 stores of 127 entries), and putting an item in when there is no more room is refused, the item staying in the pack. It does not explain the enemy cloth drops in the same report, and the link to that one case is not proven.

entries.report: Attributes or temporarily boosted skills above 99 can behave incorrectly.
entries.note: Values 98/99/100 and expiration/reapplication paths; do not assume a common cause across fields.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Attributes and skills are kept in 1..99 and 0..99 by the routines that change them, so values above 99 arise only through an attribute maximum set without its limit (B-2ffc47) or outside the game. A temporary attribute boost (R029+0x4C04) is recorded in full but added through the 1..99 clamp and the cap of maximum plus largest boost (R029+0x0A72), while its expiry takes the full amount back (R029+0x448A): a boost cut on the way up, near 99 or on top of a larger boost already running, lowers the attribute for good (B-f134d1). Whole-party boosts are registered separately (B-8b2837, B-c14d7c, B-024865); single-member skill boosts are capped to 99 before recording and are symmetric.

entries.report: Overlapping attribute blessings can leave two expiration events and subtract twice.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Each attribute blessing or potion records its own boost event, and nothing is replaced. A second boost while the first is in force records its points minus the excess over the maximum. But the attribute routine (R029+0x4E0C) caps the attribute at the maximum plus the largest single boost, so part of the recorded amount is never added. Both events later subtract what they recorded, which leaves the attribute below where it started. The mechanism is the same as RPT-EQUIP-0004, and one register entry covers both.

entries.note: Modifier-event creation, persistent armor/weapon/fire fields, equipment publication, expiration consumer, and save/reload. Reports specifically include Firewall, St. Polycarp, Deadly Blade, Greatpower, and Strongedge.

check.label: In the registers
check.original: R031+0x43B2; R029+0x4D24; R029+0x448A; R039 charm saints (St.Polycarp and others)
check.note: Deadly Blade, Strongedge and Great Power add to the member's weapon bonus byte (+0x34) and record a kind 0x4A event. When that event ends, the sheet's "Enhc/Bless" mark goes away.Hardarmor and Firewall (+0x41, +0x10) and the charm saints such as St.Polycarp record no event at all. Nothing in the game clears these bytes, which are saved with the member and read in every battle.

entries.report: Reapplying an equipment modifier can recalculate unrelated equipment.
entries.note: Reapplication dispatcher and all rewritten equipment fields.

check.label: Still open
check.note: There is no reapplication routine: each potion or saint writes the shared bytes directly. Other fields change only through carries and overwrites. Great Power and Strongedge add into the weapon byte and can carry into the damage nibble (noted in the OriginalBehaviour remarks). Hardarmor and St.Dunstan/St.Patrick add to the low nibble of +0x41, which can carry into the Firewall count. The charm saints overwrite the high nibble, and St.Polycarp overwrites the Firewall strength. The report's wording does not make clear which of these it means.

entries.report: Greatpower appears to affect the armed weapon regardless of documented category.
entries.note: Effect category predicate; may instead be a documentation mismatch.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (documentation)
check.note: Neither the potion code nor the hit code tests the weapon's kind: Great Power adds 14/22/30 to the member's weapon bonus byte (+0x34), and the hit routine (R014+0xAC08) applies that byte to every attack. The manual limits Great Power to impact weapons, flails and handguns (and Deadly Blade and Strongedge to certain kinds); the program never did, so this is a difference between the manual and the program rather than a defect of 483.07. B-23a975 covers the event type that Great Power records.

entries.report: Overlapping temporary stat effects can expire incorrectly and leave a permanent reduction below the original value.
entries.note: Test saint then potion and potion then saint, both expiration orders, and save/reload while both are active. Do not merge with `RPT-EQUIP-0001`: the visible failure and possibly the owner chain differ.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: The temporary boost (R029+0x4C04) reduces a second boost by the attribute's excess over its maximum and records the rest, as if the attribute could reach the maximum plus all boosts. The attribute routine caps it at the maximum plus the largest single boost (R029+0x4E0C). Example: with a maximum of 30, a +10 saint raises the attribute to 40; a +15 potion then records 5 but adds nothing; when both end, the attribute falls to 25. Saints and potions use the same routine, so this happens in either order.

entries.report: Battlefield-chest relic weapons are forced to quality 35 despite authored qualities.
entries.note: Chest-generation item construction and relic definition quality.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Room 14 of the Templar fortress puts three different random items from 0x96..0xAB (the relics, including the relic weapons) into its loot groups. Each is written with quality 35 (0x23) and type byte 0x9F, not with the item's own quality (50..85 for the relic weapons) or its type from DARKLAND.LST.

entries.report: Relics may not improve associated saint prayers.
entries.note: Prayer threshold inputs for ordinary and greater relics; absence across all paths is not yet proven.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (documentation)
check.note: The prayer chance depends only on the praying member's Virtue, the Divine Favor offered and the saint's own constants. R039+0x1FA0 takes a bonus argument, but all 136 saint functions pass 0. Neither the prayer screen nor the chance routines look at items, so carrying a relic does not change any prayer. Only the documentation suggests otherwise, so this is recorded as a difference between the manual and the program.

entries.report: High Sabbat can default to invalid “Jan 0” and map coordinates 0,0.
entries.note: Event initialization and failure/default record writes.

check.label: Still open
check.note: The sabbat's date and site come from a started fact (tag 1, type 4). When none exists, the date query returns day 0 of the year, printed as January 0, and the site query returns -1. The original then reads locations[-1] for the place (D-09b57b); the restoration prints nothing there. The fact is created when the sabbat quest starts (new game or the monthly check) and is renewed each time a sabbat begins, so the code does not show what removes it in play.

entries.report: High Sabbat generation fails beyond 31 December 1499.
entries.note: Calendar comparison and event generator around year 1500.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: An event created to last 'forever' (9999 hours) is given the fixed end 23:00 on 31 December 1499 (R029+0x2C4E), and the expiry pass (R029+0x3F30) ends it on 1 January 1500. The witches' sabbat quest (R039+0x1B0C) is such an event: when it ends, its facts are cleared, including the planned next sabbat. A sabbat quest started after that date already has an end in the past and expires at the next expiry pass, so no further sabbats are planned. The same limit applies to every other 'forever' event.

entries.report: Confession time can become zero near local reputation 130 and negative above it.
entries.note: Church owner arithmetic at reputation 128--132 and higher; observe the signed calendar-helper argument exactly. The report names no executable version.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Confession takes standing / -10 + 11 hours in good standing (R057+0x03CC, signed division). This gives 1 hour at standing 100..109, 0 hours at 110..119, and a negative count from 120 upward. The time routine (R029+0x54D8) adds the count to the hour without borrowing, so the clock goes back and the hour can become negative. Standing above 99 is possible because a quest's resolution adds its value without a limit (R029+0x3E06). The thresholds in the code are 110 and 120, not the reported 130.

entries.report: Tithing was reported to omit the final party member when restoring Divine Favor.
entries.note: The mined archive instead observed the Virtue increase on every eligible party member. Retain only as a boundary-test lead for parties of one through five pending exact loop inspection.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Tithing first serves the 'member' whose number is the party's best Religion value (B-f30456), and this counts as one of the party-size visits. Normally that value is above the last member number. The loop then wraps to member 0 and visits only members 0 to n-2, so the last member gets no Divine Favor; in a party of one, nobody does. The register entry covers the cause.

entries.report: Sufficient cash and Religion make Virtue gains from the church donation predictable and repeatable.
entries.note: The church takes 10% of party cash: 6,001 pf on hand produces a 601-pf donation, reported sufficient for an eligible Religion-30 character. Decode the rule; repeatability alone does not make it a bug.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (intended rule)
check.note: The church takes a tenth of the money. When that gift is over 600 pfennigs (so a purse of at least 6,010 pf), every member's Virtue rises by a thirtieth of his Religion (R057+0x067C). Religion 30 gives +1, and below 30 gives nothing. No event or cool-down limits repeats, so the gain is as repeatable as the code intends. The 16-bit purse quirks (B-42f89c and the signed low word of the tenth) are separate.

entries.report: Pause while aiming, choose Flee without a destination, then resume to release repeated missiles through the melee animation.
entries.note: Combat action state for bows, firearms, and thrown weapons. Separately observe animation, pending projectile, cooldown, original target, and target-death cleanup. Potions reportedly do not share the same autofire state.

check.label: Still open
check.note: Choosing Flee (R016+0x156E) sets the member's flee bit at once. When order mode ends with no spot chosen (R014+0xBCA8), the member keeps its current action and target. If the cursor still names the old target, the default (hand) weapon is readied while the action stays a missile action. A member with the flee bit set is skipped by the automatic engage and fight-back passes (R014+0xFADC, R014+0xFC50), and only arriving at a destination clears the bit. This could explain a shooter that keeps firing, with the melee weapon readied, but the repeated release itself has not been traced. A runtime test in 483.07 is needed: pause while aiming a bow, choose Flee, resume without clicking a spot, and watch the action word, the readied weapon and the reload timer.

entries.report: Guild/smith specialization can fail for nighttime inventories.
entries.note: Day/night merchant catalogue predicate and specialization masks.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: By day the bowyers' guild opens its shop (shop 5) with the missile-weapon categories 0x30 / 0x83C (R065+0x0F18). Woken at night, it opens the same shop with 0xFF / 0x400 (R065+0x21BC), the mask the blacksmiths', swordsmiths' and armorers' cards use. So at night the bowyers offer hand weapons and other smith goods instead of their own. The other guilds use the same mask by day and by night.

entries.report: Damage to one equipped armor copy can affect every identical stacked copy.
entries.note: Inventory aliasing/stack mutation, equipped-record identity, and damage write target.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Equipped armour is held as a type and quality only. When the armour-eating cloud (kind 4, R019+0x0300) wears it down, R019+0x0968 lowers the quality of the first pack stack with that type and quality. Identical pieces share one stack (R031+0x4A04 joins equal code, type and quality), so every spare copy in that stack is worn down with the one being worn.

entries.report: A fortress/Feste ruler can issue a raubritter quest but fail to recognize completion or pay the reward, unlike a Rathaus.
entries.note: Compare identical targets and simultaneous commissions from Rathaus, Feste, guild, Fugger, and Hanse issuers; inspect completion flags, reward owner, and reputation effects.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: The fortress offers audiences and service only in a city without a town hall (location query 0x18 = 0, R050+0x1CEE). Its commission is recorded under the same owner (0x0A) as the town hall's. Only the town hall card (R054+0x1D08) looks for a resolved commission and pays it (city size x 7 groschen). The fortress card has no such check, and a city without a town hall hides that option on the square. So a fortress commission is never paid in money. The standing and reward written when the quest resolves (R029+0x3E06) still apply. The reward card (R080+0x038C) even has a case for the fortress card (0x1B) that is never reached.

entries.report: A clerk's “come back tomorrow” appointment may establish no usable follow-up state.
entries.note: Separate the in-game appointment/event state from limitations of the third-party quest viewer mentioned in the same report.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: When the clerk (or the fortress gate) says to come back, the card shuts the place to the party (event 0x3A) until 18:00 (or 05:00). The event names expiry handler 4, which would make a 24-hour 'welcome' event (0x3B) and raise the admission chance to 99. But the event is created with flag 0, and the expiry pass (R029+0x3F30) runs a handler only when flag bit 0 is set. So the appointment leaves no follow-up state: the next visit rolls as before. No card creates 0x3B, so the 'welcome' branch of the admission chance is never reached. This concerns the game itself, not the third-party viewer mentioned in the report.

entries.report: World generation may choose a Wild Hunt banishing saint that is unobtainable anywhere in that world.
entries.note: Enumerate generated saint availability against every Hunt requirement. Random selection itself is intended; only an unavailable, ineffective, or uncleared requirement is suspect.

check.label: Still open
check.note: The Hunt's banishing saint is drawn from all 136 saints (0..135, R039+0x1F00), and only a party that knows it gets the banishing option. Monastery libraries draw their four saints from 0..134 with a generator seeded by the party and the place (R058+0x0928). Saint 135 is therefore never offered there, and each world's library saints are fixed. Other sources are a city's patron saint, the hermit by the fire (any of 0..135, at random) and a city lord's reward. Whether a given world can leave the drawn saint unobtainable depends on that world's data. Enumerating patron saints and library draws for a seed, against the drawn saint, would decide it.

entries.report: An attempted Philosopher's Stone upgrade can fail repeatedly without explaining that the university's Stone is not better.
entries.note: Separate legitimate world generation with no superior Stone from the missing comparison feedback. Do not classify it as a broken success roll without operand evidence.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (intended rule)
check.note: Each university offers a fixed stone level, ((location query 0x21 + 7) & 15) + 14, so 14..29 (R056+0x088C). A successful search upgrades the stone only when the party's stone is below that level (R056+0x0E7C). Otherwise it shows text 7, the same text as a failed search, but takes no money and no standing and opens no week-long closure. The success roll works as written; the missing 'your stone is already as good' message is a presentation matter.

entries.report: New-wind grants temporary Endurance rather than restoring lost Endurance as described.
entries.note: Potion effect vector, timed event, and description record.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (documentation)
check.note: New-wind (0x70) calls the timed attribute boost (R029+0x4C04) for Endurance. It adds 6..11, 8..13 or 10..15 points by quality band (5 above quality 45), and an event takes them back after about a day. This is the potion's coded effect, written the same way as Ironarm and Quickmove. The mismatch is with the description, which promises restored Endurance.

entries.report: Black Cloud changes no displayed Stealth/Perception and instead serves event concealment.
entries.note: Item availability contexts, event consumer, and effect vector.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (documentation)
check.note: Black Cloud (0x61) cannot be drunk, and the combat Throw list leaves it out on purpose (R019+0x0C80 skips code 0x61). Its cloud (kind 2) has no case in the cloud's effect on combatants (R019+0x0300), so it changes no attribute or skill. Card scripts use it as an event item. The code does this deliberately; the mismatch is with the description.

entries.report: Sunburst ignores range and physical obstruction while applying facing/arc logic.
entries.note: Combat target enumeration, arc predicate, distance, and line-of-sight calls.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (intended rule)
check.note: The Sunburst flash (marker type 6, R019+0x058A) acts on every able opponent of the thrower on the same floor that is not immune. It holds those whose facing is within two steps of the direction to the flash, and also the aimed-at target. It tests no distance and no line of sight: the Inside() test is applied only to the Thunderbolt and Arabian Fire blasts. The code works as written; the report describes the coded rule, not a fault in it.

entries.report: Greatpower category, expiration, and reapplication behavior contradicts documentation.
entries.note: Cross-reference `RPT-EQUIP-0001..0003`; do not create duplicate runtime policies.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: Great Power adds 14, 22 or 30 to the whole weapon-bonus byte, so its value carries across both nibbles. It records its bonus event under the pack index instead of the potion (B-23a975), and potion weapon bonuses are never undone when the event expires. So the effect has no real expiry, and drinking it again adds again without limit. The never-undone and unlimited-add parts are documented in OriginalBehaviour remarks, with no register id.

entries.report: Travel map can freeze or scroll continuously.
entries.note: World-map input and scroll controller; first exclude DOSBox/host input behavior.

check.label: Still open
check.note: Not decided from the code in this check. The travel map's input and scrolling are ported from R030 with no registered defect of this kind. A test in the original under real DOS and under DOSBox with keyboard-only and mouse-only control would separate a game fault from host input (stuck keys, mouse at the screen edge).

entries.report: A wilderness battle can begin without enemies.
entries.note: Encounter participant publication and zero-enemy continuation.

check.label: Still open
check.note: A registered original bug can produce it: when the battle loader drops an empty enemy group it also drops every group after it (B-a044f7), so if the first group on a level is empty the level has no enemies. The wilderness generator can write a group whose only kind has a count of 0 or below (R008+0x2ADC takes the second kind whatever its count), but whether a natural wilderness encounter produces such a first group was not shown. A test needs an encounter that yields that group.

entries.report: Mine Problem III parley can produce an empty screen.
entries.note: Quest event/card selection and active visual source.

check.label: Still open
check.note: The report could not be tied to a card from the code: no card resource is named for a 'Mine Problem' and the mine cards with option menus ($MineP00/01 pit traps, the mine village, the mine levels) show no registered empty-screen path. The card involved and the step reached need to be identified in a run of the original.

entries.report: The “Initial Card for Testing Only” card can appear during the main plot.
entries.note: `$INITI00` caller/owner and event-card index. Existing research must be consulted before reopening this target.

check.label: Still open
check.note: Card 0 ($Initi00, the developers' test card at R044+0x0000) is a normal entry of the card table. The only direct ways to it the restoration records are the developer stand-in card 5 (D-b8e305) and a previous-screen value of 0 (D-4d1f0e), both judged unreachable in play. Any transition to a card number held in a variable that is still 0 (a saved return card, for instance) would also open it; which one the reported case used needs a save from just before it appeared.

entries.report: Female or alchemist inn recruits can receive an incorrect sprite/color.
entries.note: Recruit template, appearance fields, palette selection, and save publication.

check.label: Still open
check.note: In the original every character who joins at an inn gets the first figure of the figure list and the inn's starting colours, whatever the character's sex or occupation (R038+0x02F8); the figure and colours are then chosen with the Select Character Image and colour keys. A female or alchemist recruit therefore starts with a default figure that may not match. Whether the report describes more than this default (for example a change after saving and loading) needs a runtime check.

entries.report: A fresh GOG game reportedly rolled from 28 July 1400 back to 1 July, repeatedly invoked copy protection, and published the first High Sabbat as “Jan 0.”
entries.confidence: moderate incident, low causal confidence; Yahoo #9692
entries.note: Treat as a possible linked initialization/state-loss cluster, not proof that every Jan-0 event shares one cause. Exercise custom-party starts from April through August 1400 while observing calendar, protection state, event initialization, and quest reset.

check.label: Still open
check.note: The code asks the copy-protection question whenever the protection event (kind 0x63) is not in the event log, and records it for 0x3E80 hours when answered (R030+0x0000; the inn records it for 0x2D0 hours). Repeated questions therefore point to that event being lost, which fits a loss of game state rather than a calendar fault, but the date rollback and the 'Jan 0' date were not explained from the code. A controlled start from April to August 1400 in the original, watching the event log and the date, would decide it.

entries.report: `$REVOL00` conditionally opens on card 5 rather than card 0 when byte `DS:5835h` is nonzero, although that byte sits between the initialized `$Revol00` and `$Revol01` resource strings and has no direct absolute writer in the current 135-overlay materialization.
entries.confidence: strong read/card relation; low defect confidence
entries.note: Identify every indirect producer or alias of `DS:5835h`, the intended lifecycle of card 5, and a controlled original transition with the byte zero and nonzero. Do not call the card dormant or expose it unconditionally meanwhile.

check.label: Still open
check.note: Confirmed read: $Revol00 (R048+0x0000) uses option block 5 instead of 0 when the byte DS:5835 is not zero. The byte is 0 in the program's initial data and no instruction in the overlays writes it by address, so the restoration always uses block 0 (a comment at RevolutionHouseByDay.cs:23, no register entry). An indirect writer (a copy or string operation running over that address) has not been excluded, so whether block 5 is ever used in play remains open.

entries.report: The nineteen-resource, 230-card city-revolt family may have been more fully connected in an earlier Darklands release and become partly or wholly dormant by 483.07.
entries.confidence: strong shipped-content evidence; no version-difference proof
entries.note: Acquire an authenticated earlier executable and matching MSGFILES; compare hashes, resources, state/event producers, dispatch owners, publication writes and `DS:5835h`; demonstrate natural unpatched entry in both versions before calling this a regression. Current 483.07 bytes prove only specific unpublished `$REVOL00/$REVOL01` rows, not whole-family dormancy.

check.label: Still open
check.note: A question about earlier releases, which the 483.07 code cannot answer. In 483.07 the revolt house cards are ported, and specific branches that are never reached are registered one by one (for example the never-enabled options of the revolt houses); whether the whole family is reachable was not established here. An authenticated earlier executable with its MSGFILES is needed for a comparison.

entries.report: In two damaged final-era saves, the party color block was displaced by exactly one 16-bit word; its trailing bytes overwrote the beginning of character record 0. Repositioning the block repaired both saves.
entries.confidence: very strong signature; trigger unknown; Groups.io #9968
entries.note: Byte-diff the party header and first character record across 4-to-5 recruitment, dismissal, temporary absence/imprisonment, death, inventory mutation, and intervening saves. Do not claim that party size or inventory quantity is the trigger until reproduced.

check.label: Still open
check.note: The save routine (R037+0x2ACE) writes the party size, the character count, the five slot ids, the figure codes (20 bytes) and the 0x78-byte colour block one after the other, then each character record, flushing before every record write; read as ported, it cannot place the colour block one word late while leaving the records in place, and the loader (R037+0x8ED4) reads the same fixed layout. The source of the displacement in the two saves is therefore not found in the save code; a byte comparison of saves around recruitment, dismissal, imprisonment and death in the original is still needed.

entries.note: Artwork/manual error, not a world-data defect if the game records are correct.

entries.report: A purchased formula belongs to the purchasing character; a traded formula goes to the current leader
entries.note: Character-owned formula knowledge is intentional according to the archive. The collective-looking interface communicates ownership poorly.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (intended rule)

The interface does not make the ownership obvious, but the code does what it was written to do.

entries.report: The main-quest fortress monastery disappears after an attempt
entries.note: Reported to reappear after a later Sabbat. Record a defect only if the intended lifecycle fails to respawn it.

check.label: Still open
check.note: The fortress monastery's place record is changed by cards (for example R122+0x0000 turns it into an ordinary place once the demon is banished), but the path by which an attempt hides it and a later Sabbat brings it back has not been traced in the code.

entries.report: Tarnhelm interaction causes the party to “crash through the floor”
entries.note: This is a scripted trap, not a software crash. Purifying the tomb, including through Transformation, is part of the intended route.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (intended rule)
check.note: A scripted card event described in the game's text, not a program crash; the item-quest crypt can also be purified with a saint or a potion as an intended route (CryptUnderTheRuinedChurch.cs, R108+0x084E, R108+0x0A5E).

entries.report: Different Wild Hunts require different randomly selected saints
entries.note: Random choice is intended. Investigate only unavailable saints, ineffective valid saints, or a Hunt that fails to clear after success.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (intended rule)
check.note: Intended: when the Wild Hunt quest is created (R087) its saint is drawn as rnd(0x88), any of the 136 saints, and its item at random; the Hunt card then offers that saint (R060+0x0978). A Hunt whose saint the party cannot get is the random draw, not a fault.

entries.report: Protection prompts occur at every map event after editing a save
entries.note: Yahoo #9643 explicitly ties this case to Jugglindan's editor. Keep separate from the fresh-GOG calendar/protection incident in `RPT-CALENDAR-0001`.

check.label: Not a bug of 483.07 (third-party tool)
check.note: Tied to a third-party save editor. The game asks the protection question on entering the map only while event 0x63 has not been started, and then records that event for 0x3E80 hours (R030+0x0000); a save whose event list was altered, or left without a free slot, can bring the question back each time. The question itself is not asked in the restoration (D-f4c0e9).

earlier_findings.title: TACANIM terminal lookup consumes inherited size words
earlier_findings.summary:
Status: byte-confirmed behavior; possible original bug, defect classification pending. R25 owner `[0A84,0BE4)` (original EXE `[54DA4,54F04)`, SHA256 `70DDC4CBF52145D75ED347ACDD294CFE139CED4EFA6B49ACF38B226336C7AA02`) checks FILE+6 bit10 at0AC8, ignores fread's result after0AD7, and compares the partially overwritten fourteen-byte local record at0AE7. A mismatch loops back to the flag test; initially terminal FILE state skips read and compare. Close0AF4 precedes size reads atBP-12h/-10h/-0Eh and their ordered reservations. Thus absent or short unmatched TACANIM records can use inherited allocation size bytes, rather than returning a lookup failure. No failed-open/read owner result is inferred from this behavior.

This appears anomalous because resource absence can affect allocation sizes through unrelated stack history. An upstream guaranteed matching record or restricted resource contract may explain ordinary safety; neither licenses zeroing the inherited words. Rewrite disposition: replicate in isolated Lane-A research with explicit inherited scratch/FILE inputs; production unchanged. Unbound bytes stop at their first actual consumer, preserving close and any earlier reservation publication. Native open/read error-state continuation remains an explicit typed stop. The campaign's controlled original comparison and tests are linked in [the current report](research/COMBAT_READER_STARTUP_CLOSURE_CAMPAIGN.md). Controlled malformed-resource inputs do not establish natural reachability.

check.label: In the registers
check.note: The size lookup in TACANIM.DB ignores the result of the read, so for a family missing from the file it keeps the last record read. The restoration records this as a known original bug and, as a deliberate fix, uses the animation header's sizes for a missing family (D-e758be).

earlier_findings.title: item-feature scratch shuffle does not select the item
earlier_findings.status: byte-confirmed redundant shuffle; defect classification pending
earlier_findings.summary: After swapping scratch-pool entries, the routine reloads the draw index at `421E`, not a pool value. Dispatch permits repeated entries; the pool has no observable influence on selection. The semantic compiler removes its scratch writes but retains saved-draw dispatch, decreasing bounds and the four-item stop. DKSAVE8's complete feature records and publication RNG falsify a shuffled pool interpretation. Repeats could be intentional: a defect verdict needs an established inventory policy and controlled original examples of repetition.
